item.title: The Cursed History of Star Brightness
item.author: explanaria@gmail.com (explanaria)
item.description:
Point at a star. How bright does that star look?
It sounds like a simple question, but when I tried to understand how we measure star brightness, I discovered a story of decades-old misinformation, rabbit holes of sexism, and at least two standards whose names have stories of their own.

item.title: There's Zero 0^0s (Unless We Choose One)
item.author: explanaria@gmail.com (explanaria)
item.description:
What is 0^0, and why do people keep saying it's "undefined"?
Isn't math all about definitions? Are the mathematicians hiding their secrets from us laypeople again? Math can't define this basic three-character symbol? Clearly it's just zero! Or maybe one! It should have some simple answer!

item.title: The Case of the Impossible Triangles: The Congruent Number Problem and Elliptic Curves
item.author: explanaria@gmail.com (explanaria)
item.description: Can you find a right triangle with area 30 whose side lengths are all rational numbers? This problem is called the "congruent number problem". Sounds simple, right? But as it turns out, solving this problem leads to some very interesting areas of math. In particular, the congruent number problem has tons of interesting connections to number theory and these things called elliptic curves, which are one of applied math's biggest success stories.

item.title: How Mathematicians Think About Four Dimensions
item.author: explanaria@gmail.com (explanaria)
item.description: The fourth dimension. Even if you barely touch math, you've probably heard the phrase before. Maybe you've heard it's space? Or time? Perhaps you've heard a radio show about how apparently some phycisist theorizes the world is actually secretly an 18.5-dimensional spiderweb. Fourth dimensions pop up all the time in science fiction, sometimes under the guise of "alternate dimensions", or even "parallel dimensions". But what does it mean? How do you work with it?
